Theme

Latin word

prīmum

adverb; followed by deinde, tum, postrēmō

first, firstly, in the first place; for the first time (with a word of time: tum, nunc, hodiē)

In this lexicon

  • firstly

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. B.G. 1.25: Caesar prīmum suō, deinde omnium ē cōnspectū remōtīs equīs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 3.7.1; Traupman 40; Traupman 69; Traupman 61: prīmum omnium, first of all; Traupman 315

  • for the first time

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.7.12: lūdōrum grātiā quōs tum prīmum anniversāriōs in circō facere cōnstituisset (Lewis & Short s.v. tum); Ter. And. 5.4.33: post illa nunc prīmum audiō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 315; Traupman 316, 394

  • ubi prīmum (ut prīmum, cum prīmum): as soon as

    classical

  • ut prīmum (cum prīmum, simul ac): moment

    classical

Examples

  • prīmum est dēvium, deinde ab Autrōniō et cēterīs quadriduī, deinde sine tē.

    Firstly, it’s off the road; secondly, it’s four days from Autronius and the rest; and thirdly, it’s without you.Cic. Att. 3.7.1

    In the entry for firstly

  • prīmum omnium ego ipse vigilō

    first of all, I am awake myselfCic. Cat. 2.19 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for firstly

  • ante omnia nē sit vitiōsus sermō nūtrīcibus

    above all, the nurses’ speech must be free of faultsQuint. 1.1.4

    In the entry for firstly

  • hoc ante omnia fac, mī Lūcīlī: disce gaudēre

    do this before all else, my Lucilius: learn to be gladSen. Ep. 23.3

    In the entry for firstly

  • prīncipiō

    for startersTraupman 384

    In the entry for firstly

  • pōnte sublicio tum prīmum in Tiberī factō

    the Pile Bridge having then for the first time been built over the TiberLiv. 1.33.6 (Lewis & Short s.v. tum)
